Scheme 1998 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Scheme'), upholding the order dated 10.02.2021 passed by Sub Divisional Collector, Anni, District Kullu, H.P., whereby the claim of the petitioner for grant of alternative land in addition to compensation awarded in his favour in terms of provision contained in the scheme, came to be dismissed, petitioner approached this Court in the instant proceedings filed under Article 227 of the Constitution of India, praying therein for following relief:-

"It is therefore, respectfully prayed in this premise that this petition may kindly be allowed throughout and to quash and set aside the order of Sub Divisional Collector Anni (Annexure A-7) and Deputy Commissioner Kullu (Annexure A-8) and direct the .
respondent No.1 to make allotment of land to the petitioner in view rd of the Notification dated 3 March 2017 Notification No.Rev- D(G)10-9/2016 (Annexure A-1) in a time bound manner in the interest of justice and fair play."
2.

Precisely, the facts of the case as emerge from the record are that the land of the petitioner was acquired for Defence purposes at village Averi, District Kullu, H.P., and in lieu of acquisition,
compensation worth Rs. 6,01, 360/- was also paid to him.

Though, petitioner was satisfied with the compensation, as detailed hereinabove, but being aggrieved on account of non-grant of alternative land in addition to compensation as per the policy of 2017, he filed petition/application before Sub Divisional Collector, Anni, District Kullu, H.P., praying therein to allot 5 biswas of land in addition to compensation in terms of the Scheme, wherein provision came to be made for allotment of alternative land in addition to compensation in favour of those persons, who on account of acquisition of their land became landless.

sentences.text: At this stage, it may be noticed that before filing aforesaid petition in the Court of Sub Divisional Collector, Anni, District Kullu, H.P., petitioner approached this Court by way of CWP No.3860 of 2020, which came to be disposed of vide order dated 23rd September, 2020, reserving liberty to the petitioner to file representation to the competent authority with the direction to such authority to decide the same within a period of six weeks.

In the aforesaid background, Sub Divisional Collector,
Anni, District Kullu, H.P., vide order dated 10.02.2021 though considered the representation of the petitioner made pursuant to order dated 23.9.2020 passed by this Court, but rejected the same on the ground that on account of acquisition of land at village Averi, petitioner has not become landless.

. 
3. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the aforesaid order passed by Sub Divisional Collector,
Anni, District Kullu, H.P., petitioner filed an appeal under Section 10 of aforesaid scheme before Deputy Commissioner Kullu, but same was also dismissed vide order dated 24.3.2022.
In the aforesaid background, petitioner has approached this Court in the instant proceedings.

4. Having heard learned counsel representing the parties and perused material available on record,
especially reply filed by the respondents, this Court finds that the facts, taken note hereinabove, are not in dispute.

It is also not in dispute that entire land of the petitioner at village, Averi came to be acquired for Defence purposes and on account of acquisition of land, petitioner has already received compensation to the tune of Rs. 6,01, 360/- .

5. Precisely, the grouse of the petitioner as has been highlighted in the instant petition and has been further canvassed by learned counsel for the petitioner is that apart from compensation, petitioner Krishan Lal vs Deputy Commissioner & Others on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53442916/
2 is also entitled for allotment of 5 biswas of land in terms of the Scheme formulated by Government of Himachal Pradesh.

sentences.text: Mr. Susheel Gautam, learned counsel for the petitioner while making this Court peruse Scheme vehemently argued that as per Clause-4 of aforesaid scheme, an Oustee or his family who have been rendered the landless as a result of acquisition of land is entitled to land equivalent to half of the land acquired subject to maximum limit of 2 bighas.

He submitted that in the case at hand petitioner is entitled to allotment of 5 biswas of land on account of his having been rendered .
landless.

6. Learned counsel representing the petitioner further argued that reply filed by the respondents itself suggests that on account of acquisition of land of the petitioner in village Averi, he has rendered landless and as such, entitled for allotment of land in addition to compensation.

He stated that number of similar situate persons, who had rendered landless in village, Averi on account of acquisition but had land in other parts of the State were allotted plot in addition to compensation.

7. Mr. B.C.Verma, learned Additional Advocate General, while refuting aforesaid submission made by learned counsel for the petitioner argued that on account of acquisition of land in village, Averi petitioner has not rendered landless and as such, he is not entitled for allotment of plot in addition to compensation already received by him qua acquisition of land.

He also submitted that besides above, petitioner is not eligible to be allotted plot on account of the fact that he is not permanent resident of the village Averi, which is the condition precedent for allotment of plot.

He further contended that neither petitioner is having any dwelling house and cattle shed in village, Averi nor Doghary and as such, no illegality can be said to have been committed by the Courts below while rejecting the prayer of the petitioner for allotment of land in addition to compensation already received by him.
8.

Before ascertaining the correctness of rival submissions made by learned counsel for the parties,
this Court deems it fit to take note of relevant paras of the Scheme, which reads as under:
.

"3. Purpose for which land may be granted:-
Land may be granted to an ouster for dwelling house Agriculture/Horticulture purposes, provided he is eligible for the grant of land under this scheme.
4.

The maximum limit for grant of land on ouster:-
 i) An Oustee or his family Equivalent to half of the land Krishan Lal vs Deputy Commissioner & Others on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53442916/
3  who have been acquired subject to rendered the landless maximum limit two bighas.

as a result of  acquisition of land.
ii) An Ousted of his family Equivalent to the land is permanent resident acquired subject to r of village Averi and his maximum limit of 10 biswas.
dwelling house only has been acquired.

`
iii) An Oustee or his family Equivalent to the land who is not permanent acquired subject to the resident of village Averi maximum limit of 5 biswas.
and his doghary/cattle shed only has been acquired.
Provided that an Oustee, who has received compensation of Rs. 5 lac or above, shall not be entitled for the grant of land under this para.

Provided further that the remaining land(after allotment the Oustee) shall be reserved for common purpose like construction of dispensary/school, Mahila Mandal, Panchayat Bhawan etc."
9.

Careful perusal of Clause-3 of the Scheme suggests that land shall be granted to an ouster for dwelling house Agriculture/Horticulture purposes, provided he is eligible for the grant of land under this scheme.
Eligibility for grant of land has been provided in Clause-4.

As per aforesaid Clause, an Oustee or his family who have been rendered landless as a result of acquisition of land shall be entitled to land equivalent to half of the land acquired subject to maximum limit of 2 bighas.

An Oustee or his family, .
who is not permanent resident of village Averi and his doghary/cattle shed only has by acquired shall be entitled to land acquired subject to maximum limit of 5 biswas.

10. Initially, it was provided in the scheme that an Oustee, who has received 5 lac shall not be entitled for grant of land under aforesaid para, however such condition was subsequently removed vide communication 3.3.2017, issued under the signature of Deputy Secretary ( Revenue) to the Government of Himachal Pradesh, which is reproduced hereinbelow:-
"No. Rev-D(G)10-9/2016 Government of Himachal Pradesh Department of Revenue(D-Section) From The Additional Chief Secretary (Revenue) to the Government of Himachal Pradesh, Shimla-2.

 District Kullu, Himachal Pradesh,
 rd  Dated:-Shimla-2, 3 March, 2017  Sub:- Regarding allotment of land at Village Averi, Tehsil Nirmand,
District Kullu, H.P. under the rehabilitation Scheme for oustees/displaced persons.
Sir, I am directed to refer to your letter No. 2214/DRA Dated 05.10.2016 on the subject cited above and to say that after consideration in the matter, it has been decided by the Government that the cases of the left out Oustees/affected persons/families of Averi Village including those who have received the compensation amount of Rs. 5.00 lacs or above at lest for 0-05-00 bighas (five biswa)
may be considered for the allotment of land/plots out of the acquired land surrendered/made available by the Govt. of India, Ministry of defence, New Delhi at village Averi, District Kullu for R&R purpose of Oustees Averi village in relaxation of first proviso below the then sub Divisional Officer (Civil) Ani, as per clause/Rule-7 under the Resettlement and Rehabilitation of Oustees of village Averi (Grant of land)
Scheme 1998.

With the issuance of aforesaid communication, persons having received compensation of Rs. 5 lacs or above also became entitled for allotment of land/plots of land/plots out of the acquired land surrendered/made available by the Govt. of India, Ministry of Defence, New Delhi at village Averi,
District Kullu, H.P.
It is not in dispute that on account of acquisition of land of the petitioner at village Averi, he has left with no land at village Averi and as such, entitled for allotment of plot.

Though, word "landless" has not been defined in the scheme but in definition clause contained under Clause 2 word 'Oustee' has been defined as under:-

sentences.text: 5 "2. Definitions:-
In this scheme unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context, the following shall have the meanings assigned to below:-

(i). Oustees: For purpose of this Scheme means a person who has been deprived of his house, land or bold, on account of acquisition proceedings in connection with the Defence Establishment and entitled to compensation in lieu thereof and includes his successors in interest.

(ii). Family: Means husband/ wife of the ouster, their children including step or adopted children and includes his parents and those brothers and sisters who were living and cultivating and jointly with him before acquisition.

(iii) Existing: Means the holding possessed by the family of an ouster immediately after acquisition of his property."
12.

As per aforesaid definition, "Oustees" would be a person who .
has been deprived of his house, land or bold, on account of acquisition proceedings in connection with the Defence Establishment and shall be entitled to compensation in lieu thereof.

If aforesaid definition is read in context of provision made in Clause-4 for allotment of land in addition to compensation, there appears to be merit in the contention of learned counsel representing the petitioner that an "Oustee" or his family, who have been rendered landless on account of acquisition of land in village Averi, shall be entitled for allotment of land apart from compensation.

"Landless person" has been defined in the scheme called Himachal Pradesh Grant of Nautor land to landless and other eligible persons scheme 1975, which reads as under:-
"Landless persons means person who holding no land for agriculture purposes,
whether as an owner or a tenant earns his livelihood principally on manual labour on land and intends to take the profession of agriculture and is capable of cultivating the land personally.

Other eligible persons has been defined as a person who hold land less than one acre in the State of H.P. as a landowner or a tenant and earns his livelihood principally or manual labour on land and intends to take the profession of agriculture and is capable of cultivating the land personally and includes those land owners who were either rendered landless or whose holding were reduced to less than one acre as a result of implementation of the Himachal Pradesh Abolition of Big Landed Estates and Land Reforms Act, 1953."
13.

sentences.text: Interestingly, in the reply filed by the respondents, though it has been stated that the petitioner has been neither rendered landless due to acquisition nor there was any house/cattle shed and Doghary of the petitioner existing on the aforesaid land, but no document has been adduced on record to suggest that petitioner possesses some other land other than acquired for the Defence purposes.

6 14.

sentences.text:
Though, Mr. B.C.Verma, learned Additional Advocate General .
argued that since petitioner is not permanent resident of village, Averi and had no dwelling house or cattle shed on the land acquired, he is otherwise not entitled to allotment of land as per the scheme,
but this Court finds no force in the submission of learned Additional Advocate General for the reason that provision contained in Clause 4 of the scheme itself suggests that an "Oustee" or his family who have been rendered landless as a result of acquisition of land in village Averi is entitled to land equivalent to half of the land acquired subject to maximum limit of two bighas.

Separate provision has been made in sub clause 3 of Clause 4 of the Scheme with regard to an Oustee or his family, who is not permanent resident of village Averi and his Doghary /cattle shed only has been not acquired.
In that situation an Oustee or his family would be entitled to allotment of land equivalent to the land acquired subject to maximum limit of 5 biswas.
Case of the petitions falls in the aforesaid category, who is not resident of village, Averi, but his land has been acquired for Defence purposes.

Though, landless person has been not defined in the scheme and definition of landless, as has been provided under Nautor Rules, is of not much relevance as far as present case is concerned but in the facts and circumstances of the case, "Oustees" defined in Clause-2 shall be entitled to alternative plot in terms of Clause 4 of the Scheme, if it is so, then petitioner being permanent resident of village, Averi becomes entitled for allotment of land in terms of sub Clause 3 of Clause 4, which provides that an Oustee or his family, who is not permanent resident of village,
Averi shall be entitled for allotment of land equivalent to the land acquired subject to .
the maximum limit of 5 biswas.

15. Though, at this stage, learned Additional Advocate General vehemently argued that since Doghary/cattle shed of the petitioner never came to be acquired, he is not entitled to allotment of land in terms of sub clause 3 of Clause 4 of the scheme, but this Court having read the scheme in its entirety, finds that very object and purpose of promulgation of this Scheme is to provide alternative land to a person, whose land is acquired for public purposes.
In the instant case, it is not in dispute that entire land of the petitioner situate in village, Averi has been acquired for Defence purposes, as a result of which, he has been rendered landless.

No doubt, petitioner has already received compensation qua the acquired land, but such fact cannot be a ground to deny his right flowing from scheme, which entitles him for allotment of land in addition to the compensation.

16. Consequently, in view of the above, the present petition is allowed and orders dated 10.02.2021 passed by Sub Divisional Collector, Anni and order dated 24.3.2022 passed by Deputy Commissioner, Kullu, District Kullu, H.P., are quashed and set-aside.
The respondents are directed to allot land to the petitioner as per his entitlement in terms of the scheme in addition to compensation, which has been already received by him.
Since petitioner has been fighting for his rightful claim for years together, this Court hopes and trusts that needful shall be done by the respondents within a period of eight weeks.
Pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.

(Sandeep Sharma), .
